findings.message: Nil pointer dereference: cfg.ProducerPrivKeyRange is used without checking if it's empty, causing panic when Trim on empty string in edge cases
findings.suggestion: Add a check for empty string before trimming: if cfg.ProducerPrivKeyRange == "" { return privateKeys } before the Trim call

findings.message: Race condition: blocklisteners slice is modified during iteration in RemoveBlockListener without proper synchronization, causing potential slice corruption or panic
findings.suggestion: Move the slice modification logic outside the loop by collecting indices first, then remove in reverse order after releasing the lock

findings.message: Blocking operation in hot path: SendBlockToSubscribers blocks indefinitely on channel send without timeout, causing deadlock if subscriber is slow
findings.suggestion: Use non-blocking send with select and timeout: select { case elem.pendingBlksBuffer <- blk: default: log.Warn("subscriber buffer full") }

verdict.summary: The review session successfully identified and addressed critical concurrency and edge-case bugs across two key files. The coder consistently applied targeted fixes and correctly rejected false positives in later rounds, especially regarding the non-blocking channel send pattern. However, repeated findings on the same lines across rounds suggest the reviewer may not have fully verified the applied fixes before re-reporting.
recommendations: Add unit tests specifically for edge cases in config.go:142 (e.g., whitespace-only ProducerPrivKeyRange) to prevent regression
Document the locking strategy in pubsubmanager.go comments to clarify why slice modification during iteration is safe (write lock held throughout)
Consider adding a timeout-based test for SendBlockToSubscribers to verify non-blocking behavior under load
